title: Administrative Action on Canonical Configurations
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, and let $w,u$ be Boolean words. Choose a saved configuration of $M$ on input $w$, semantic states $q,q'$, natural numbers $i,i'$ with $i,i'\le |w|$, integer offsets $j,j'$, and signs $m,d\in\{-1,0,1\}$. If moving the input head from position $i+1$ by $m$ gives position $i'+1$, and $j+d=j'$, then applying the administrative action with input move $m$, certificate-head move $d$, no emitted bit, and target state $q'$ to the canonical evaluation configuration determined by the saved configuration, $u,q,i,j$ gives the canonical configuration determined by the same saved configuration and $u$, with state $q'$, input position $i'$, certificate-head offset $j'$, and empty output.
hypotheses_covered: finite Boolean machine $M$ with $k$ work tapes
replaced:
Applying a non-emitting administrative evaluator action to a canonical evaluation
configuration yields the canonical configuration with the prescribed new control
state, the input position moved as stated, and the certificate head displaced by
the stated amount; the saved extractor bank and the empty output are preserved.
